\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{परिणामः} (pariṇāmaḥ)}{परिणामः (pariṇāmaḥ)}]{\sk{परिणामः} (pariṇāmaḥ) — a result}

\label{lesson:SA-C169-parinamah}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for a colour, then the Sanskrit for a word.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{परिणामः}}
\textbf{\sk{परिणामः}} — \emph{pariṇāmaḥ} — \textquotedblleft{}a result\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{pariṇāma} comes from \emph{pari-√nam} \textquotedblleft{}bend round, change, ripen\textquotedblright{}, the root √nam \textquotedblleft{}bend\textquotedblright{} with \emph{pari} \textquotedblleft{}around\textquotedblright{} (MW): \textquotedblleft{}change, transformation, ripening\textquotedblright{}, and so \textquotedblleft{}the outcome, the result\textquotedblright{}. It is the root √nam of \emph{namaste}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pariṇāmaḥ}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Sanskrit for a colour, then the Sanskrit for a word, then say \emph{pariṇāmaḥ} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{अंकः} (aṅkaḥ)}{अंकः (aṅkaḥ)}]{\sk{अंकः} (aṅkaḥ) — a mark, a number}

\label{lesson:SA-C169-ankah}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for a word, then the Sanskrit for a result.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{अंकः}}
\textbf{\sk{अंकः}} — \emph{aṅkaḥ} — \textquotedblleft{}a mark, a number\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{aṅka} comes from the root √añc \textquotedblleft{}bend, curve\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 100): first \textquotedblleft{}a hook\textquotedblright{} in the Rigveda, then \textquotedblleft{}a curved line, a mark\textquotedblright{}, and so \textquotedblleft{}a numeral\textquotedblright{}. MW compares Greek \emph{ankōn} \textquotedblleft{}elbow, bend\textquotedblright{} and Latin \emph{uncus} \textquotedblleft{}hook\textquotedblright{}, and it lives on as Hindi \emph{āṁk} \textquotedblleft{}mark\textquotedblright{} and Punjabi \emph{aṅg} \textquotedblleft{}figure\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 100).
\end{cousinweb}

\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{श्रेणी} (śreṇī)}{श्रेणी (śreṇī)}]{\sk{श्रेणी} (śreṇī) — a row, a grade}

\label{lesson:SA-C169-sreni}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for a result, then the Sanskrit for a mark.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{श्रेणी}}
\textbf{\sk{श्रेणी}} — \emph{śreṇī} — \textquotedblleft{}a row, a grade\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{śreṇī}, also \emph{śreṇi}, \textquotedblleft{}a line, a row, a series\textquotedblright{} is old, in the Rigveda. The grammarians derive it from the root √śri \textquotedblleft{}lean on, attach\textquotedblright{} (MW), and CDIAL 12718 suggests the same with a query, so its origin is not settled. \textquotedblleft{}Grade\textquotedblright{} is its school use today.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{शब्दकोशः} (śabdakośaḥ)}{शब्दकोशः (śabdakośaḥ)}]{\sk{शब्दकोशः} (śabdakośaḥ) — a dictionary}

\label{lesson:SA-C169-sabdakosah}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for a mark, then the Sanskrit for a row.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{शब्दकोशः}}
\textbf{\sk{शब्दकोशः}} — \emph{śabdakośaḥ} — \textquotedblleft{}a dictionary\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{śabdakośa} is built from \emph{śabda} \textquotedblleft{}sound, word\textquotedblright{} and \emph{kośa} \textquotedblleft{}a vessel, a store, a treasury\textquotedblright{} (MW): \textquotedblleft{}the word-store\textquotedblright{}. MW already records it as the name of a dictionary, and \emph{kośa} \textquotedblleft{}treasury\textquotedblright{} is the usual Sanskrit word for a lexicon.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{लेखनम्} (lekhanam)}{लेखनम् (lekhanam)}]{\sk{लेखनम्} (lekhanam) — writing}

\label{lesson:SA-C169-lekhanam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for a row, then the Sanskrit for a dictionary.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{लेखनम्}}
\textbf{\sk{लेखनम्}} — \emph{lekhanam} — \textquotedblleft{}writing\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{lekhana} comes from the root √likh \textquotedblleft{}scratch, write\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 11103): first \textquotedblleft{}scraping\textquotedblright{} in the medical books, then \textquotedblleft{}writing\textquotedblright{}. \emph{lekha} \textquotedblleft{}a letter\textquotedblright{} and \emph{lekhanī} \textquotedblleft{}a pen\textquotedblright{} come from the same root.
\end{cousinweb}
